data.name: SurrealVR
data.detailed_description:
Surreal VR


Giant emojis? Check. Robot puppies? Check. Avatars? Check. Doodle with friends? Check. Come hang out in a surreal, magical place being built by people who love virtual reality, gaming, and buzzing dinosaurs with flying drones.

Welcome to crazy, fun and social world of SurrealVR.

Version 3.0


There are big changes in SurrealVR with our latest update.

Finally, Oculus Touch Support!


  • Cross Platform between Vive, Oculus and PC
  • VR, NoneVR, Motion Controllers (Vive and TOUCH) and also Gamepad support

New Avatars!


  • Realistic or cartoony avatars, human, alien or robot… We have them all now
  • From head to toe, customize your avatar and make your own VR identity
  • New teleportation system (Classic walk is also supported)
  • Voice chat, IK, lip sync

Game Trailers, Drones and Brush!


  • Video player in Home scene with game trailers to watch
  • Identity Sync with games powered by SurrealVR
  • Play Drone Fighters on Steam and use same identity back and forth
  • Get game points with actions and mini games
  • Spend your game points to customization
  • Real time networked physics objects, throw, catch, shoot
  • Use Surreal BRUSH for creating things together
  • Whiteboard location to share drawings
  • Fly a RC drone in VR
  • If that’s not enough Fly a human size drone in Dino Location

Do you want to win an award?


We hide a crazy secret in Surreal. Some things you can find in Surreal world and solve an impossible puzzle. What is it? What to do with it? We can’t say. You should figure it out. If you are the first one to solve, you will win something BIG. It is extremely difficult we must admit, so reward is equally awesome.

Location Location!


  • Home
  • Cruise Ship
  • Dinosaur Island
  • Drone Fighters Preview
  • Basketball Court
  • Zombie Shooting
  • Whiteboard
  • Psychiatric Ward
  • Dance Club
  • Dadaism
  • Confession Room

reviews.review:
SurrealVR is an imaginative social virtual reality experience that combines multiplayer interaction, exploration, creative activities, and experimental entertainment within an unconventional digital playground. Developed and published by Surreal Games, this free-to-play title emphasizes freedom and social engagement rather than traditional objectives or storytelling. Players are encouraged to explore unusual environments, customize their virtual identities, interact with objects, and participate in recreational activities. Its greatest attraction lies in the freedom to experiment with different experiences, although the overall execution occasionally struggles to match the ambition behind its concept.

The game's central feature is its multiplayer social environment, where players can communicate and participate in shared activities. Support for HTC Vive, Oculus hardware, conventional PC gameplay, motion controllers, and gamepads demonstrates an effort to accommodate different hardware configurations. Voice communication, avatar lip synchronization, and inverse kinematics help make virtual interactions more expressive. These systems are particularly important in an experience where social engagement forms the foundation of entertainment. However, the quality of the experience depends considerably on finding other participants, since many activities become less engaging when explored alone.

Avatar customization adds personality to the virtual world by allowing players to select from human, alien, robotic, and cartoon-inspired characters. The ability to modify appearances encourages individuality and provides a sense of identity during multiplayer sessions. This feature complements the game's social focus, making interactions more memorable when players encounter unusual or humorous character designs. Although the customization system offers entertaining possibilities, it lacks the sophistication and extensive creative freedom associated with more advanced social VR platforms.

Environmental variety is among SurrealVR's strongest qualities. Players can explore locations such as Dinosaur Island, a cruise ship, a basketball court, a dance club, a zombie shooting area, and several stranger environments inspired by surrealist concepts. Each location introduces a different atmosphere or activity, encouraging curiosity and experimentation. Dinosaur Island stands out through its flying drone mechanics, while the basketball court and zombie shooting activities offer more conventional entertainment. The confession room and collaborative whiteboard provide alternatives centered on communication and creativity. Unfortunately, the individual environments can feel relatively shallow, with limited objectives and insufficient complexity to sustain prolonged engagement.

Interactive physics contribute significantly to the game's playful personality. Players can throw, catch, and manipulate objects through networked interactions, creating opportunities for spontaneous entertainment. Remote-controlled drones introduce another enjoyable activity, including the unusual possibility of operating a human-sized flying machine. These mechanics demonstrate how virtual reality can transform otherwise simple actions into entertaining physical experiences. Nevertheless, the novelty of these interactions may diminish over time, especially when the surrounding environments lack meaningful challenges or progression.

Creative tools provide another interesting dimension through Surreal BRUSH and shared drawing spaces. These systems allow participants to collaborate on artwork, exchange ideas, and create humorous visual experiments. The collaborative approach suits the game's emphasis on social freedom, offering activities that do not depend on competition or mechanical skill. A basic progression system also rewards participation with points that can be spent on customization. Additionally, the presence of a hidden puzzle introduces an element of mystery, encouraging players to investigate their surroundings more carefully. However, these features function primarily as supplementary attractions rather than substantial standalone gameplay systems.

Visually, SurrealVR embraces a colorful and deliberately eccentric aesthetic. Giant emojis, robotic animals, dinosaurs, and exaggerated character designs contribute to an atmosphere that celebrates absurdity and imagination. Its artistic direction prioritizes playful experimentation over realism, which works reasonably well for a virtual social playground. However, the visual presentation can appear inconsistent across locations, and some environments lack the polish expected from more refined virtual reality experiences. The graphical quality is functional rather than exceptional, with environmental detail and animation sophistication occasionally falling behind the creativity of the underlying concepts.

Movement options include teleportation and conventional walking, allowing players to choose between different navigation preferences. Teleportation is particularly beneficial for individuals susceptible to motion discomfort, while traditional movement provides greater control during exploration. The game also supports non-VR interaction, broadening accessibility beyond dedicated headset owners. Nevertheless, its technical design reflects an earlier generation of virtual reality software, and modern hardware compatibility may vary depending on drivers, operating systems, and peripheral configurations. Multiplayer functionality also depends on reliable network connectivity and the continued availability of supporting online services.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially listed as Unsupported. Players primarily interested in experiencing it on Valve's handheld should keep this limitation in mind rather than assuming that the simple controls automatically guarantee full compatibility. Its design may appear ideal for portable play, but the official Deck classification does not currently provide that assurance.

The most noticeable limitation is the lack of substantial long-term progression. While the game offers numerous activities, many function as brief distractions rather than fully developed gameplay experiences. Its entertainment value also depends heavily on an active community, since exploring empty social spaces can quickly become repetitive. The game's mixed Steam reception reflects its divisive appeal, suggesting that its creative ambitions resonate with some players while its technical and gameplay limitations discourage others. Nevertheless, its free-to-play accessibility makes experimentation relatively approachable for anyone curious about unconventional social VR experiences.

Overall, SurrealVR is an inventive but uneven virtual playground that succeeds more through creativity and variety than mechanical sophistication. Its customizable avatars, unusual environments, collaborative activities, drone mechanics, and physics-based interactions create an appealing foundation for casual social entertainment. However, limited gameplay depth, inconsistent presentation, uncertain online activity, and compatibility concerns prevent it from becoming a consistently engaging experience. It remains worth exploring for players interested in experimental virtual worlds, particularly those who enjoy spontaneous multiplayer interactions and unconventional digital environments. 

Rating: 6/10
